Check and render an edited write-up again

Source: R/doc-synth-recheck.R
gr_recheck.Rd

gr_synthesise() keeps $text_marked, the write-up with its [study N] markers, so that the checks can be run again on the text as published. Edit that text, by hand or with another tool, and pass it here: every check that reads the text runs on it again, and the citations and the reference list are rendered from it as gr_synthesise() renders them. Nothing is sent to a model.

Usage

gr_recheck(synthesis, text_marked = synthesis$text_marked)

Arguments

synthesis

A gr_synthesise() result.

text_marked

The edited write-up, in the marker form of synthesis$text_marked: citations as [study N], sections under ## headings, and no reference list (one is appended from what it cites). Defaults to synthesis$text_marked, which renders the write-up again.

Value

The gr_synthesis, with text_marked the edited text, text rendered from it, and references, figures, sentences, uncited and contradictions worked out again, and recheck, a list of unknown (studies cited that are not in the table), unsupplied (studies cited under a heading whose section was not shown them) and unparsed (citations the check cannot read).

Details

The checks are those of gr_synthesise(). A marker naming a row that does not exist, or a study the section under whose heading it stands was not shown, is left as a marker and counted; one the check cannot read is counted. Each is warned about (gr_recheck_citations). A heading the write-up did not have is checked against every study any section was shown. A study cited honestly under one heading keeps its rendered citation and its reference even where another heading cites it without being shown it. The figures are checked against the rows their sentence cites, with the style and figure_bands the write-up was made with, as the revised text of a write-up is (stage "edited" in $figures); the sentences are linked to verified records again; and $uncited and $contradictions are worked out again. The sections, their counts and $draft are left as written: they describe the draft, not the edit. For a synthesis saved before $section_studies was kept, shown in $uncited is NA, since what each section was shown is not known. A synthesis saved by an earlier version comes back with the fields added since filled with their defaults: no studies lost or left unrendered, and the citation style and bibliographic columns it was written with.

See also

gr_synthesise()

Examples

tab <- data.frame(document = c("a.pdf", "b.pdf"), status = "ok",
                  n_filled = 1L, n_unverified = 0L, n = c(120L, 300L))
cl <- hr_mock_client(function(messages, params) "One trial enrolled 120 people [study 1].")
s <- gr_synthesise(tab, question = "How large were the trials?",
                   outline = c(Findings = "Sample sizes"), client = cl)
#> [1/1] Findings
edited <- paste0(s$text_marked, " Another enrolled 300 [study 2]. A third [study 9].")
r <- suppressWarnings(gr_recheck(s, edited))
r$recheck$unknown
#> [1] 9
r$uncited
#> [1] study       document    document_id shown      
#> <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)
